principles: Keep JSON stdout machine-readable and put progress on stderr or a structured side channel.
Make progress events real-time and flushed so parent lastActivity sees them.
Separate command timeout semantics from idle liveness.
Use host-neutral process and lock ownership checks.
drivers: story_advance --phase=TEST must not kill active validate work merely because stdout is quiet.
lattice validate --json consumers must still parse stdout reliably.
Forced exits and stale locks must not create misleading test failures or block retries.

options.name: progress-stderr-plus-parent-idle-refresh
pros: Works with existing parent output-based idle watchdog
cons: Requires careful tests around stream separation and buffering
Requires touching both validate runner and lifecycle runner integration

options.name: disable-or-extend-idle-watchdog-for-validate
pros: Avoids false idle kills for long validate runs

options.name: write heartbeat only to a temp file or lock metadata
cons: Parent watchdog may not observe it without polling changes
Does not directly solve output-silence killing

rationale: Choose JSON-safe stderr progress and heartbeat consumed by the parent idle watchdog because it fixes the observed idle-kill while preserving fail-closed command timeout behavior and parseable JSON output.

preMortem.trigger: Progress is written to stdout in --json mode
preMortem.mitigation: Route JSON-mode progress to stderr and add parseability tests around stdout.

preMortem.scenario: Heartbeat accidentally grants unlimited command runtime
preMortem.trigger: Idle refresh also resets timeoutMs accounting
preMortem.consequence: A hung command can run forever
preMortem.mitigation: Track per-command wall-clock timeout independently and test timed commands still fail.

preMortem.scenario: Forced exit leaves a fresh-looking lock
preMortem.trigger: Parent kills child without cleanup or PID is reused
preMortem.consequence: Later validate runs are blocked or misclassified
preMortem.mitigation: Use owner token/start metadata/host-neutral liveness checks and stale-lock tests.

preMortem.scenario: Runner failure is reported as ordinary test failure
preMortem.trigger: Evidence writer collapses watchdog timeout into test assertion failure
preMortem.consequence: User debugs tests instead of infrastructure
preMortem.mitigation: Introduce/verify infra_failure classification for lifecycle runner failures.
